entities.summary: Stanley Ben Prusiner is an American neurologist and biochemist. He is the director of the Institute for Neurodegenerative Diseases at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF). Prusiner discovered prions, a class of infectious self-reproducing pathogens primarily or solely composed of protein, a scientific theory considered by many as a heretical idea when first proposed. He received the Albert Lasker Award for Basic Medical Research in 1994 and the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1997 for research on prion diseases developed by him and his team of experts beginning in the early 1970s.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Prusiner's discovery of prions revolutionized the understanding of infectious diseases and led to significant advances in neurodegenerative disease research, with his work on prion diseases contributing to a deeper understanding of the causes of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease and other fatal brain disorders.
